content:
You are revising a resume that has already been written. Change as little as possible.

THE DRAFT (its summary, and each role with its bullets):
[[draftJson]]

TERMS THE RESUME IS MISSING. Each of these is on the target job's checklist, or was taken out of the skills block because it is not a tool, and a scanner counts every one:
[[missingTermsJson]]

[[figuresNote]]

[[softSkillsNote]]

[[summaryNote]]

WHAT TO DO

Work the missing terms into the summary or the bullets, spelled EXACTLY as listed above - same words, same order, same singular or plural. Capitalisation follows the sentence, not the list: a product keeps its official casing (PyTorch, TensorFlow, NumPy, JavaScript) however the list writes it, and an ordinary phrase - a soft skill, a practice - is lower case in the middle of a sentence: "time management", "accountability", never "Time management" halfway through a bullet. Attach each to work the draft already describes: a capability like "full-stack development" or "artificial intelligence" belongs inside a sentence about something that was built, never in a list and never as "experienced in".

Widen the sentences that are already there rather than adding new ones - by working the term into the action or the thing acted on, never by hanging a clause off the end of the result. A bullet may carry two or three of these terms and should still read as one thing that was done; 30-42 words is the room you have, and a role may not exceed 8 bullets.

THE ONE EXCEPTION. A term naming an INDUSTRY this candidate has not worked in - a clinical, legal, defence or trading practice on somebody who has never worked in that field - stays out. Leave it missing rather than claiming it.

WHAT MAY NOT CHANGE

Every employer, job title, date and location. Any project, client, system or outcome that is not already in the draft: you are rewording what is there, not inventing more of it. Any figure already in a sentence, unless you are asked above for more. And never add a number or a before-and-after to a bullet unless the note above asks for more figures: most bullets say what changed in words.

VOICE

Past tense, plain words, no em-dashes. Never these words in any form: leveraged, utilized, spearheaded, orchestrated, streamlined, seamless, robust, scalable, maximized, cross-functional, end-to-end, innovative, dynamic, cutting-edge, world-class, holistic, comprehensive, proven, strategic. Do not open a sentence with Designed, Architected, Led, Delivered, Drove, Integrated, Partnered, Supported, Contributed, Managed or Streamlined. Never let a bullet's verb repeat its own noun: "Automated model training workflow automation" is the shape to avoid.

THREE THINGS A REVISION MUST NOT BREAK

THE SUMMARY KEEPS ITS YEARS. If you rewrite the summary, keep the candidate's total years of experience exactly as the draft states it, as a numeral ("7 years"), within the first two sentences. Keep the summary to two or three sentences - never one. One missing term in the summary at most; the rest go into bullets.

NO SENTENCE-ENDING TAGS. Never place a term by hanging it off the end of a finished bullet: "...using problem solving and critical thinking", "...through time management and prioritization", "...through analytical thinking and problem solving", "...while maintaining accountability in written communication across reviews". A bullet ends on its result. A term that can only go in as a trailing tag stays missing.

NOTHING SAID TWICE. Never write a term into a sentence that already carries it or a form of it, never the same word or phrase twice in one sentence whatever its capitalisation ("Collaboration" and "collaboration"), and never the same phrase in two bullets; a term the page already says twice stays out. Read every bullet you changed back once: a phrase said twice is a failed check, so fix it before you return.

RETURN

Only a JSON object, and only the parts you changed:

{
"summary": "the rewritten summary, or omit this key if you did not change it",
"experience": [
{ "company": "exactly as the draft spells it", "title": "exactly as the draft spells it", "achievements": ["every bullet for this role, in order, changed and unchanged alike"] }
]
}

List a role only if you changed one of its bullets, and when you do, return ALL of that role's bullets. Return nothing else: no skills, no cover letter, no dates, no commentary.
